title: India's Blue Colts Blank Bangladesh 3-0 to Keep AFC U-20 Asian Cup Dream Alive
excerpt: Goals from Danny Meitei Laishram, Vishal Yadav, and Md Arbash sealed a convincing win in Tashkent, leaving India's first U-20 Asian Cup qualification in 20 years dependent on other results.
body:
• India U-20 beat Bangladesh 3-0 in their final Group B match at Do'stlik Stadium in Tashkent on September 6, finishing with six points from three games
  • Danny Meitei Laishram opened the scoring in the 25th minute, Vishal Yadav added an acrobatic second on the hour, and substitute Md Arbash sealed it in the 79th
  • India will qualify for the AFC U-20 Asian Cup China 2027 if Syria fail to beat group-toppers Uzbekistan — which would end a 20-year absence from the tournament
  • Head coach Mahesh Gawli made one change from the 4-0 loss to Uzbekistan, with the tactical adjustment paying off immediately

India's U-20 football team delivered a must-win performance on Sunday, blanking Bangladesh 3-0 in their final Group B qualifier at the Do'stlik Stadium in Tashkent to keep their AFC U-20 Asian Cup China 2027 hopes alive.

After a bruising 4-0 defeat to hosts Uzbekistan in their previous outing, head coach Mahesh Gawli's side needed a convincing victory to maintain any chance of qualifying — and the Blue Colts delivered with three well-taken goals across the 90 minutes.

Danny Sets the Tone

Danny Meitei Laishram broke the deadlock in the 25th minute after a high press forced a Bangladeshi defensive error. Md Abdul Riyad Fahim gave up possession cheaply under pressure, and Hateem Ali showed sharp awareness to play the ball through to an unmarked Danny inside the box. The forward made no mistake with the finish, giving India a lead they would never relinquish.

India nearly doubled their advantage before halftime when Danny stepped up for a free kick that headed toward goal, only for the Bangladesh goalkeeper to make a sharp save. The first half ended 1-0, with India the clearly dominant side.

Second-Half Surge

The Blue Colts resumed with attacking intent and were rewarded on the hour mark. Rishikanta flicked a long throw into the box, where Vishal Yadav rose above the Bangladeshi defenders to produce an acrobatic finish that left the goalkeeper with no chance. The goal doubled India's lead and visibly settled any remaining nerves.

Bangladesh pushed forward aggressively in the final 30 minutes, but India's defense held firm. The contest was effectively sealed in the 79th minute when substitute Md Arbash, who had come off the bench with fresh energy, unleashed a powerful strike that crashed off the crossbar and into the net to make it 3-0.

Qualification Hopes Rest on Syria Result

India finished Group B with six points from three matches — a 1-0 win over Syria in the opener, the 4-0 loss to group-toppers Uzbekistan, and Sunday's comprehensive victory. They are placed second in the group, but qualification is not yet confirmed.

The Blue Colts will progress to the AFC U-20 Asian Cup if they finish among the seven best runners-up across all eight qualifying groups. Their fate now hinges on the Syria-Uzbekistan match: if Syria lose or draw, India's position as one of the best second-placed teams appears secure.

A successful qualification would end a remarkable 20-year drought — India last appeared at the AFC U-20 Asian Cup in 2006. For Gawli and his young squad, the wait for confirmation will be anxious but the performance in Tashkent has given them every reason to be optimistic.

The match also exposed ongoing issues with match officiating. Multiple fouls by Bangladeshi players went uncalled throughout the game, including what appeared to be a handball inside the penalty area in the first half, costing India at least two additional goal-scoring opportunities according to Indian football observers.
